header.name: Critical Thinking
header.description: This course introduces the learner to the fundamentals of critical thinking and informal logic. We will use a ‘mixed’ instructional methodology that includes lecture, Q&A, learning team activities, discussion of videos, slides, print articles and the text.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Demonstrate the knowledge of underlying assumptions in all statements, positions and arguments.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Being able to apply the distinction between perceptions, opinions, facts, values, knowledge.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Define and recognize the stereotypes, rationalization, prejudice-- The differences and the overlap between these categories.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Practicing the art of active listening in any discussion.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: ‘loaded’ issues—political, economic, religious, and philosophical. Why a single perspective analysis often lands us in circular arguments, dogma and an inability to register or

outcomes.label: CO6
outcomes.raw_text: Uncovering common prejudices through the knowledge of semantic maps and territories.

outcomes.label: CO7
outcomes.raw_text: Demonstrate the differences between Critical and Creative Thinking -- how and why they supplement each other.

outcomes.label: CO9
outcomes.raw_text: Spot the differences between formal and informal logic.
